description: Frozen v1 support boundary for trust-operation mutation detection (issue #1714 checkpoint 1, revision 2 per the #1715 independent review). This is the reviewed boundary: a row here is support; anything outside it is unsupported by definition, not an undetected gap. Changes require an explicit reviewed diff to this file, never silent scope expansion. Revision 2 fixes: transformation_understanding=supported now REQUIRES a plan_ref to a real byte-bound plan fixture (tests/fixtures/trust_operation_v1/plans/valid/); append-shaped operations (tee -a, >>) are now unsupported_transform, not supported, because appending is categorically not the remove-only transform v1 models; the T028-vs-T002 filename-based distinction is removed in favor of plan_ref presence; T030's over-limit construction is pinned to the actually-configured max_command_length bounds in src/safety/mod.rs, not an invented number.

profiles.name: macos-bsd-cert-pem-v1
profiles.notes: Linux test runners use injected macOS-profile metadata and do not treat wheel as their native default. No Windows trust-store support is claimed in v1.

config_bounds._source: src/safety/mod.rs SafetyConfig::{strict,moderate,permissive}() and src/safety/segments.rs::MAX_DEPTH, read at the time this manifest was frozen (checked with: grep -n 'max_command_length:' src/safety/mod.rs; grep -n 'MAX_DEPTH' src/safety/segments.rs). A manifest row that needs a boundary value MUST reference one of these fields, never a new literal.

rows.description: Single-quoted literal install(1) with BSD -m/-o/-g forms targeting the named profile path. Command-text fixture only (no bound plan): the write-shaped operation is identified, but without plan.schema.json byte-level evidence the transformation it performs is unknown, not supported.

Double-quoted literal cp(1) with explicit -f source/destination onto the named profile path, bound to a real plan fixture (tests/fixtures/trust_operation_v1/plans/valid/mutating_removal_with_backup_required.json) whose approved_removal_ranges resolve against real artifact bytes under tests/fixtures/trust_operation_v1/artifacts/. This is the one command-text form in this manifest allowed to claim transformation_understanding=supported, and it is allowed only because a real plan backs it — not because of the command syntax alone.

cp(1) with -p preserving metadata, zsh dialect, literal paths. Command-text fixture only: no bound plan, so transformation understanding is unknown, matching T001/T002's distinction (plan_ref presence, not filename or form, decides supported vs unknown).

tee -a append redirection onto the named profile path. Append is a categorically different transformation kind than remove_approved_certificates_only (it can only add bytes, never remove an approved certificate occurrence), so transformation_understanding is unsupported here regardless of any plan — v1 has no transformation model for append at all. Previously (revision 1) this row incorrectly claimed transformation_understanding=supported; that was the #1715 review's point 5 finding.
Plain >> append redirection onto the named profile path. Same reasoning as T004: append cannot imply a supported remove-only transform.

Plain > truncating redirection onto the named profile path. A truncating write replaces the whole file like cp/install, but (like T001/T003) this row carries no bound plan, so transformation_understanding is unknown rather than supported.
sudo prefix wrapping a supported install(1) form. No bound plan on this row specifically (T002 is the one plan-bound row); unknown, not supported.
env prefix wrapping a supported cp(1) form.
command prefix wrapping a supported install(1) form.
Absolute declared executable path form of install(1).
Literal sh -c payload carrying a supported form. Used as the base row for T032's wrapper-depth boundary construction below.
Repeated path separators and a trailing . component on the destination, lexically normalized to the profile target.
Relative destination resolved against an explicitly supplied cwd matching the profile target directory.
Parent-directory traversal (..) that lexically resolves onto the profile target.
Write-shaped operation with a protected-target token but incomplete supported resolution: cp into a variable-free but non-enumerated option form.
Supplied context maps an opaque destination variable name to the protected target, but the mapping itself is not resolvable from the command text alone.
Benign control: read-only cat of the profile target, no write-shaped operation.
Benign control: sha256sum hashing the profile target for inspection, no write.
Benign control: copying the bundle out to a scratch path for later inspection; destination is not the protected target.
Unsupported: shell alias expansion stands between the literal text and the real destination.
rows.verdict_floor_note: Alias expansion is out of scope for trust-operation detection, but this does NOT relax the existing safety validator's own pattern-based risk assessment of the literal text; any existing ask/deny verdict from src/safety/ is preserved independently of this contract.

rows.description: Unsupported: shell function expansion stands between the literal text and the real destination.
rows.verdict_floor_note: Same fail-closed note as T020: function expansion is undetected by this contract, but the existing safety validator's verdict on the literal text is unaffected.

rows.description: Unsupported: live symlink resolution required to know the destination is the protected target. The symlink-to-target mapping below is context_provenance=supplied_fixture: it exists ONLY so this fixture can exercise the not_detected path deterministically. A real run performs no symlink resolution and has no such mapping (context_provenance=unobserved in production); v1 ships no live resolver.
Unsupported: variable substitution in the destination with no supplied context binding.
Unsupported: command substitution computing the destination dynamically.
Unsupported shell dialect (fish) for an otherwise-supported form.
rows.verdict_floor_note: fish is outside the declared shells list, so trust-operation detection is not_detected here. This is conservative-by-omission, not conservative-by-override: it does NOT itself downgrade or bypass any existing ask/deny verdict the safety validator's pattern matching already applies to this literal text in a fish context; that existing fail-closed behavior is unchanged and untouched by this contract.

rows.description: Unsupported option form: install(1) long-option equivalents of -m/-o/-g are not in the enumerated form list.
Unsupported profile: a Windows certificate-store target is out of scope entirely in v1.

Same cp(1) form as T002, deliberately using a neutral filename, with NO bound plan. Fixes the #1715 review's point 5 finding: revision 1 distinguished T028 from T002 purely by giving this row's source file a suggestive name ('fully-untrusted-bundle.pem'), which is not a real detection signal. T002 and T028 are now identical in command shape; the ONLY difference is plan_ref, and that difference is exactly what correctly separates supported from unknown.
Relative destination with no supplied cwd: scope cannot be established.

Over-limit input: deterministically constructed by right-padding T002's literal command with spaces to exactly one byte past the STRICT safety level's configured max_command_length (config_bounds.max_command_length_strict + 1 = 1001 bytes), so the boundary is reviewable and reproducible instead of an invented number. Fixes the #1715 review's point 6 finding (revision 1 invented '4096' against the actually-configured 1000/5000/10000).

Filename-renaming control: identical cp(1) form and identical lack of a bound plan as T028, with yet another filename, to demonstrate that the verdict tracks plan_ref presence and command shape, never the filename string. T002, T028, and T031 together show: same shape + plan_ref -> supported (T002); same shape, no plan_ref, ANY filename -> unknown (T028, T031).

Wrapper-depth boundary: T011's sh -c payload nested one level past the existing wrapper-scan depth bound (config_bounds.max_wrapper_depth = 3, src/safety/segments.rs::MAX_DEPTH), constructed deterministically (wrap T011's full command in another literal sh -c '...' layer, repeated until nesting_depth = max_wrapper_depth + 1 = 4) rather than hand-typed. Beyond the bound, the innermost command's write-shaped operation is out of the declared scan depth: not_detected, unsupported_syntax.

Plan-bound no-op: identical command shape to T002/T031, bound instead to the no-op plan fixture (plans/valid/no_op_targets_absent.json) where the before snapshot already lacks both approved targets. mutation_detection stays identified (it is still a recognized write-shaped operation against the protected target) and transformation_understanding stays supported (a real plan backs it, with approved_removal_ranges of count=0), independent of whatever postcondition.effect a later run would report (already_satisfied).
